fulltext: Samsung Newsroom
on November 19, 2026

Samsung Electronics is once again connecting K-pop fans worldwide by livestreaming 2026 MAMA AWARDS. Through a partnership with CJ ENM, a leading Korean entertainment company, Samsung TV Plus will broadcast the entire two-day event, with CHAPTER 1 taking place on November 20 and CHAPTER 2 on November 21.
2026 MAMA AWARDS will air live on the CJ ENM K-POP channel in 14 countries,1 featuring performances by some of K-pop’s biggest stars.
Held at Kyocera Dome Osaka in Japan, 2026 MAMA AWARDS kicks off on November 20 with the red carpet at 3:30 p.m. Korea Standard Time (KST), followed by the awards show from 6 p.m. to 9:30 p.m. KST.

Special collaborations will bring this year’s awards’ “A MUSIC INTERSTELLAR” theme to life. Under the slogan “All Generation,” this year’s MAMA AWARDS aim to connect K-pop’s past, present, and future by uniting artists, genres, artistic forms, and fans. Highlights include BIGBANG and Dooly the Little Dinosaur, ENHYPEN and “Dune: Part Three,” and Panic and younger K-pop artists’ special collaboration with WOODZ and members of CORTIS, ZEROBASEONE, ALLDAY PROJECT, and Hearts2Hearts.

The “Art Meets MAMA” project will further reflect the “All Generation” slogan by showcasing the work of acclaimed Korean contemporary artist Lee Bae onstage. Through themes of disappearance, creation, time, and cycles, the project will explore the enduring power of music.

“Samsung TV Plus is giving fans around the world a front-row seat to one of K-pop’s biggest celebrations,” said Hun Lee, Executive Vice President of Visual Display (VD) Business at Samsung Electronics. “Together with CJ ENM, we’re bringing fans two unforgettable days of live performances and special collaborations they can enjoy from the comfort of their homes.”

To catch every moment, viewers can set reminders on their Samsung TVs to tune into the CJ ENM K-POP channel on November 20 at 3:30 p.m. KST and November 21 at 12:30 p.m. KST for CHAPTER 1 and CHAPTER 2, respectively. While watching, they can adjust their TVs’ sound and lighting settings to recreate the atmosphere of the awards show at home.

2026 MAMA AWARDS are the latest addition to Samsung TV Plus’s extensive lineup of Korean content. With more than 100 million monthly active users and availability in 30 countries, the free ad-supported streaming service continues to expand its premium entertainment offerings, making Korean entertainment accessible to audiences worldwide.

三星电子通过直播 2026 年 MAMA AWARDS 再次连接全球韩国流行音乐粉丝。通过与韩国领先的娱乐公司 CJ ENM 合作，三星 TV Plus 将直播整个为期两天的活动，其中 CHAPTER 1 将于 11 月 20 日举行，CHAPTER 2 将于 11 月 21 日举行。
2026 MAMA AWARDS 将通过 CJ ENM K-POP 频道在 14 个国家/地区直播1，其中包括一些韩国流行音乐巨星的表演。
2026 年 MAMA AWARDS 在日本大阪京瓷巨蛋举行，将于 11 月 20 日下午 3:30 走红地毯，拉开帷幕。韩国标准时间 (KST)，随后下午 6 点开始颁奖典礼。至晚上 9:30韩国标准时间。

特别合作将今年的奖项“音乐星际”主题变为现实。今年的 MAMA AWARDS 以“All Generation”为口号，旨在通过联合艺术家、流派、艺术形式和粉丝来连接 K-pop 的过去、现在和未来。亮点包括 BIGBANG 和 Dooly the Little Dinosaur、ENHYPEN 和“Dune: Part Three”，以及 Panic 和年轻韩国流行艺术家与 WOODZ 以及 CORTIS、ZEROBASEONE、ALLDAY PROJECT 和 Hearts2Hearts 成员的特别合作。
“艺术遇见MAMA”项目将通过在舞台上展示著名韩国当代艺术家李裴的作品，进一步体现“All Generation”口号。该项目将通过消失、创造、时间和循环等主题，探索音乐的持久力量。
三星电子视觉显示 (VD) 业务执行副总裁 Hun Lee 表示：“三星 TV Plus 为世界各地的粉丝提供了前排座位，观看韩国流行音乐最大的庆祝活动之一。” “我们与 CJ ENM 一起，为粉丝们带来两天难忘的现场表演和特别合作，他们可以在舒适的家中享受。”
为了捕捉每一刻，观众可以在三星电视上设置提醒，以在 11 月 20 日下午 3:30 收听 CJ ENM K-POP 频道。 KST 及 11 月 21 日中午 12:30分别适用于第 1 章和第 2 章的 KST。在观看时，他们可以调整电视的声音和灯光设置，以在家中重现颁奖典礼的氛围。
2026 MAMA AWARDS 是 Samsung TV Plus 丰富的韩国内容阵容的最新成员。这家免费的广告支持流媒体服务每月拥有超过 1 亿活跃用户，覆盖 30 个国家/地区，并不断扩大其优质娱乐产品，让全球观众都能享受韩国娱乐。

fulltext: IT之家 11 月 19 日消息，《21 汽车 · 一见 Auto》昨日报道称，理想汽车与宁德时代之间维持多年的供应关系，在 2026 年秋季走到了一个微妙的临界点。
今年 9 月初，理想先是以 26.5 亿元增资欣旺达动力，随后宣布全系车型切换自研电池。官宣次日，宁德时代 A 股股价下跌 3.65%，市值缩水 540 亿元。外界将此视为双方“切割”的信号，但两家公司对外口径始终一致：仍是战略合作伙伴。
《一见 Auto》指出，双方真正的裂痕始于 2025 年第四季度的 i6 电池供应。当时理想向用户承诺年底提车可配备宁德时代电池，意味着宁德是 i6 该季度的电池独供方。理想 10 月下发的产能指标为 8000 个电池包，宁德实际只交付了 4000 个，理由是“产能不够”。i6 在国庆期间积累的约 4 万台订单，2025 年内只交付了 2.9 万台，约 1 万台被迫推迟至 2026 年交付。
一位车企电池高管对此的评价是，供应商产能偏差超过 50% 属于“巨大的供应失误”。李想在那段时间几乎每天都在焦虑电池产能，核心焦虑在于“命运掌握在别人手里”。
宁德方面也有其难处。2025 年 9 月宁德产能利用率已达 96.9%，产线两班倒之外加开第三班，接近满产。在产能紧缺时，宁德内部按合作关系分级，同为优先保障级别的情况下，会优先向有资本绑定的车企倾斜。理想虽长期属于最高等级的客户，但双方始终未建立股权层面的绑定。
如果说 i6 断供动摇了理想对供应确定性的信任，那么 2025 年 11 月的 MEGA 召回则触及了责任划分的底线。一辆 2024 款 MEGA 在行驶中起火，调查指向同批次冷却液防腐性能不足，极端情况下可能导致动力电池热失控。理想决定召回 11411 辆 2024 款 MEGA，免费更换冷却液、动力电池及前电机控制器。
在召回前的沟通会上，宁德方面建议单点解决、不进行大规模召回。理想高管当场反问：如果再出现一台自燃车辆，宁德能否与理想共同承担责任？据在场人士描述，宁德方面未作回应，会议不了了之。
理想最终执行了召回。财报上的损失为 11 亿元，但内部人士透露实际花费超 20 亿元，全部来自公司现金流。业内人士测算，单台召回成本最高可达 15 万元，涉及电池更换及关联冷却部件的工时费用。
这次事件之后，理想内部的复盘结论指向同一个方向：关键零部件的供应与责任，必须回到自己手中。

在资本层面，理想的动作在 2026 年 9 月密集落地。9 月 4 日，理想以 26.5 亿元增资欣旺达动力，交易完成后合计持有后者约 11.17% 股份。更早的 2025 年 10 月，双方已以 50:50 比例合资成立山东理想汽车电池有限公司，承接自研电池的生产制造。自研电池并非从电芯到整包的全链条自制，电芯由欣旺达与中创新航代工，理想深度介入材料规格、工艺参数与全流程数据，电池包则由理想自研自制。
10 月 20 日，理想正式发布“连山”电动技术体系，并推出电池保障计划：因自研电池质量问题引发自燃且车辆达到报废标准，赔付同等配置新车。MEGA 搭载的连山电池容量 108kWh，CLTC 续航 710km，5C 超充规格与宁德时代版本在纸面指标上保持对齐。
同时，宁德时代也在调整。2026 年 10 月，换电业务负责人、时代电服 CEO 杨峻接替韩伟兼任市场体系联席总裁，乘用车 CTO 高焕接棒国内乘用车业务副总裁王慧的职责。选择更熟悉车企体系的高管主管乘用车业务，被外界视为对当前客户关系变化的回应。
除理想外，小米也推出了自有电池品牌“龙甲电池”，电芯由中创新航、欣旺达等提供，小米把控全流程；鸿蒙智行则通过巨鲸电池平台引入国轩高科、中创新航等多家供应商。

fulltext: IT之家 11 月 19 日消息，美国当地时间 11 月 18 日周三召开的 DealBook 峰会上，OpenAI 首席执行官萨姆 · 奥尔特曼（Sam Altman）表示，其公司正在“安全”与“发展”寻找 AI 平衡点。
奥尔特曼和 OpenAI 总裁格雷格 · 布罗克曼（Greg Brockman）共同参与本次活动，他们表示在推进 AI 发展的进程中不可避免地会遇到风险，因此公司必须在优先保障安全和持续创新之间做出取舍。
奥尔特曼在访谈中坦言，OpenAI 不可能“让所有人都满意”。他称，如果公司只顾“踩满油门”追求技术突破，公众会担心人工智能失控；但若过度强调安全，也可能延缓产品和技术进步。
奥尔特曼强调 OpenAI 采取“迭代部署”策略，即分阶段推出技术、在真实环境中观察风险并不断改进。在他看来，理解 AI 风险的重要方式之一，不能完全脱离实际进行封闭开发，更重要的是让技术接受现实检验。
奥尔特曼也承认，随着模型能力迅速增强，安全、对齐和监控的难度正在显著提高。OpenAI 总裁、联合创始人格雷格 · 布罗克曼表示，随着模型能力显著增强，安全性、保障性和“对齐”（即 AI 行为符合人类意图）已成为必须认真对待的问题。他称，这不只是 OpenAI 一家公司的转变，更是整个 AI 行业正在经历的文化转变。
OpenAI 已与其他 AI 公司签署自愿协议，承诺开展风险评估，并与第三方评估机构合作。该公司本周表示，正在引入 METR、Apollo Research 等机构的独立安全研究人员，对模型进行安全评估。
奥尔特曼还警告，当前 AI 公司之间的激烈竞争不利于安全。他表示，各家公司只能了解自身的安全标准，难以充分掌握竞争对手的开发情况；这种“迷雾中的竞赛”可能使安全投入不足。他呼吁行业建立共同的安全标准，并推动更大程度的透明度。
针对硅谷部分关于 AI 逐步接管决策权、甚至可能形成“超级智能”的讨论，奥尔特曼明确表示反对。他说，人类必须继续掌控未来，不应将决策权逐步交给 AI；布罗克曼也认为，AI 能力越强，保障其与人类目标一致、安全可控的责任就越大。
在商业层面，奥尔特曼透露 OpenAI 仍计划在某个时点上市。此前，OpenAI 已将 IPO 计划推迟至明年，以优先处理安全问题；本月早些时候，公司完成 110 亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 734.89 亿元人民币）融资，估值达 1.25 万亿美元（现汇率约合 8.35 万亿元人民币）。

Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella explained Wednesday why he offered buyouts to 60,000 of his employees in October, essentially urging them to voluntarily quit instead of reducing the workforce via another massive layoff.

Short answer: AI, but not, he insists, in the way you might expect. He’s not saying he’s replacing employees with AI, especially software engineers. He’s saying he’s reorganizing Microsoft into a company where everyone uses AI to do their work, and their jobs become focused on managing that AI.
The buyout was “to make sure that at least everyone felt like they had agency in making choices,” he told Andrew Ross Sorkin during the DealBook Summit.

“Let’s take software engineering. We went from, ‘Well, we don’t buy that AI can ever do software.’ To suddenly, ‘Wow, it can do all software, and why do we need software engineers?’ To now rediscovering that software engineering is very much alive and, in fact, is going to thrive, except the way the team is organized and the work that a software engineer does has now got a new operating point,” he explained.
For some people, “that reorganization and change is sort of hard, right?” he added, “but, I mean, it has to be done.”

He offered the example of the team that builds Cowork, the AI agent in Microsoft 365 apps. He said the team consists of just 11 developers who have mastered using AI to do their jobs. “They build a software factory that builds the product. They don’t build the product.”

He believes that every employee will one day similarly become a manager of agents, rather than a person directly doing the work. “That level of direction is what, by the way, is going to happen in all jobs.”

But Microsoft, as a 51-year-old company, didn’t grow up as an AI-first company. “So the question is, how quickly can an incumbent transform the work, the workflow, and the work artifact, and with all the wage support that goes with it?” he said. “It’s going to take a bit more time than anyone expects. And there is going to be in all of this, you know, people who may say, ‘Hey, I have some other choices I want to make.’”

When asked about this same topic — why ask 60,000 people to voluntarily resign — last week by Gergely Orosz on his The Pragmatic Engineer podcast, Nadella further explained, “We have created enormous anxiety in people sort of feeling that they don’t have control of their own destiny because the way we have talked about this AI revolution.”

He called out talk about the singularity (the hypothetical point at which AI surpasses human intelligence) and predictions that AI will take away all jobs. “All of that leads anyone who even wants to change to be sort of anxious … You have to sort of walk the hard walk of really making the structural changes, getting people slotted, giving them opportunity.”
In other words, the buyout was the message to employees: You can get with the new AI-first program, which will radically change your job, or you choose to get on with your life. Elsewhere.

微软首席执行官萨蒂亚·纳德拉 (Satya Nadella) 周三解释了为什么他在 10 月份向 6 万名员工提供了买断计划，实质上是敦促他们自愿辞职，而不是通过另一次大规模裁员来减少员工数量。
简短的回答是：人工智能，但他坚持认为，人工智能的方式并不像你想象的那样。他并不是说他要用人工智能取代员工，尤其是软件工程师。他说他正在将微软重组为一家每个人都使用人工智能来完成工作的公司，并且他们的工作重点是管理人工智能。
他在 DealBook 峰会上告诉安德鲁·罗斯·索金 (Andrew Ross Sorkin)，这次收购是“为了确保至少每个人都觉得自己在做出选择时有代理权”。
“以软件工程为例。我们从‘好吧，我们不认为人工智能可以做软件。’突然之间，‘哇，它可以做所有软件，为什么我们需要软件工程师？’现在重新发现软件工程非常活跃，事实上，它将蓬勃发展，除了团队的组织方式和软件工程师所做的工作现在有了一个新的操作点，”他解释道。
对于一些人来说，“重组和改变有点困难，对吧？”他补充道，“但是，我的意思是，这必须完成。”
他提供了构建 Cowork（Microsoft 365 应用程序中的 AI 代理）的团队的示例。他表示，该团队仅由 11 名开发人员组成，他们已经掌握了使用人工智能来完成工作。 “他们建立了一个软件工厂来构建产品。他们不构建产品。”
他相信，每一位员工有一天都会同样成为代理商的经理，而不是直接做工作的人。 “顺便说一句，这种程度的指导将在所有工作中发生。”
但微软作为一家拥有 51 年历史的公司，并不是一家以人工智能为先的公司。 “所以问题是，现任者能够以多快的速度改变工作、工作流程和工作工件，以及随之而来的所有工资支持？”他说。 “这将比任何人预期的要花更多的时间。你知道，在这一切中，人们可能会说，‘嘿，我还有一些其他的选择要做。’”
上周，当盖尔盖利·奥罗斯 (Gergely Orosz) 在他的务实工程师播客中被问及同一主题——为什么要求 60,000 人自愿辞职时，纳德拉进一步解释道，“我们已经让人们产生了巨大的焦虑，他们感觉自己无法掌控自己的命运，因为我们谈论人工智能革命的方式。”
他呼吁谈论奇点（人工智能超越人类智能的假设点）以及人工智能将夺走所有工作的预测。 “所有这一切都会导致任何想要改变的人都感到有点焦虑……你必须艰难地真正进行结构性改变，让人们进入岗位，给他们机会。”
换句话说，这次买断是向员工传达的信息：你可以接受新的人工智能优先计划，这将从根本上改变你的工作，或者你选择继续你的生活。别处。

fulltext: IT之家 11 月 19 日消息，当地时间 11 月 16 日，微软 CEO 萨提亚 · 纳德拉在接受《The Pragmatic Engineer》播客节目采访时谈到了一些大家关心的问题。
当被问及公司面向约 6 万名员工推出自愿离职计划，是否意味着微软将借助 AI 提高效率并进一步裁员。
对此，纳德拉没有直接给出肯定或否定的答复，而是坦言，随着 AI 改变软件开发方式，微软员工的工作模式和团队组织结构都将发生变化。
纳德拉表示，微软希望旗下超过 20 万名员工都能继续成长，但公司需要以不同方式重新配置员工队伍。他指出，未来仍然存在大量职业发展机会，不过这些机会的具体形态可能有所不同，包括团队规模、工作流程以及岗位职责等方面。
“我也希望自己能够坐在这里告诉大家，一切都会保持原样。但我做不到。”
纳德拉承认，微软内部并非所有团队都已经适应 AI 带来的变化。他表示，不希望员工被困在一个没有完成转型的团队中，即使这个团队属于微软内部也是如此。如果员工感觉自己的职业发展受到限制，可以选择离开当前团队。不过，他更希望员工能够在微软内部寻找其他发展机会。
这次采访由前微软工程师 Gergely Orosz 主持。面对有关自愿离职计划是否预示 AI 相关裁员的问题，纳德拉强调，公司希望给予员工更多自主权，让他们能够进入符合自身长期职业发展和经济利益的岗位。
纳德拉还提到，系统工程师、基础设施人员以及 AI 训练研究人员等岗位的薪酬正在大幅上涨。微软希望通过相关安排，让员工有更多机会转向这些需求增长的领域。他同时表示，前向部署工程师（FDE）是微软目前增长最快的岗位之一。
IT之家此前报道，微软于 2026 年 10 月 26 日正式公布自愿离职计划（Voluntary Exit Offer，简称 VEO）。微软首席人力资源官 Amy Coleman 表示，该计划面向美国、加拿大、英国和印度部分参与团队中职级为 70 级及以下的符合条件员工，提供经济补助和职业规划支持。具体参与范围由各业务部门根据业务优先级、客户承诺和人员需求决定。
据《财富》杂志报道，微软方面确认约有 6 万名员工符合此次计划的申请条件，并预计实际肯接受其离职条件的人的比例低于 5%，即不足 3000 人。微软方面表示，推出计划并不意味着希望大量员工离开，而是希望让合适的人才进入合适的岗位。
这项计划与微软此前推出的自愿退休计划有所不同。今年 4 月的自愿退休计划仅面向美国员工，并要求员工年龄与在微软服务年限之和达到 70 年；此次 VEO 则没有年龄和工龄门槛。
Gergely Orosz 随后也在 X 上分享了自己对这次采访的理解。他预计，微软接下来可能进行规模较大的组织调整，逐步以原生 AI 团队作为新的组织模式。他还认为，自愿离职计划也可能促使一些认为自己所在团队缺乏转型进展的开发人员考虑外部机会。
AI 已经在改变微软的软件开发流程。纳德拉此前透露，AI 生成的代码已经占微软代码总量的 20% 至 30%。微软杰出工程师 David Fowler 也曾表示，手动编写代码的传统工作方式正在发生变化。
纳德拉认为，随着代码生成成本不断下降，软件开发的难点正在转向验证环节。他表示，在代码生成已经变得廉价的情况下，如何验证代码正确性，反而成为更加困难的问题。
对于微软是否会恢复应届毕业生招聘，纳德拉承认公司目前放缓了相关招聘工作。他表示，微软首先需要重新调整现有员工的岗位配置，将员工安排到更适合的团队，然后再考虑增加校园招聘。
纳德拉还谈到了 AI 对未来软件工程团队组织方式的影响。他认为，未来的 AI 原生企业可能从一名员工和一定数量的 AI Token 预算开始，随着工作量增加，再逐步引入更多人员。不过，他也强调，现在判断这种模式是否会成为长期趋势还为时过早。
纳德拉最后承认，科技行业围绕技术奇点以及未来工作岗位可能消失等话题的讨论，已经给从业者带来了巨大的焦虑。对于微软此次获得自愿离职资格的约 6 万名员工而言，公司高层对 AI 转型和组织调整的表态，也意味着微软未来的岗位结构和团队工作方式可能继续发生变化。

During his appearance at The New York Times’ DealBook Summit on Wednesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella lamented the fact that a lot of America’s software systems — including those governing everyday hardware and transportation systems — suffer from unfixable software vulnerabilities that, in the age of AI-aided cyberattacks, are just waiting to be exploited.

“Remember, there is a lot of stuff in our critical infrastructure that’s unpatchable,” Nadella said. “I mean, think about all the firmware and the chillers [a cooling device often used in data centers] and the HVAC systems everywhere else. So all of that, by the way, they’re on the internet.”
In other words: The smartification of the economy, in which much of the world’s “dumb” devices were hooked up to the internet, is now causing tremendous headaches.

The conversation took place against the backdrop of a wave of recent large-scale outages — including one involving Microsoft Outlook. Others have involved the NSA, the FFA, and Apple. Concerns have swirled that these outages are the result of cyberattacks, although officials have denied those claims. Still, the reality of AI-aided cyberattacks is spurring companies to find new strategies for vulnerability discovery and remediation.
Nadella touched briefly on the recent Outlook situation, noting that the global inconvenience was the result of a “latent bug” that led to a “perfect storm.”
“We put out an incident response, and we’re going to obviously take all of the learnings, both upstream architectural, as well as operational, and fix that,” he added.

“Somebody was telling me about sort of even the transportation systems and the amount of stuff that’s discoverable but with unpatchable firmware,” Nadella also added on the topic of vulnerable systems. “So we’ll have to really modernize for sure … and then we will have to assess what the threat vector looks like, what our own ability to both detect and then defend in real time looks like.”

Nadella made a broader point as well, which is that the process of patching software vulnerabilities has escalated to match the speed of potential exploitation, but that this has caused more problems.

“We now have a very powerful tool that finds vulnerabilities,” he said. However, companies used to have more time to test those patches, understand a situation, and deploy them, he said. At the same time, AI has made sophisticated cyberattacks much easier to enact.
“The patch [now] needs to go instantly from being available to being patched in production, because it’s being exploited in the wild, right? So that’s going to create instability.”

“请记住，我们的关键基础设施中有很多东西是无法修补的，”纳德拉说。 “我的意思是，想想其他地方的所有固件和冷却器（数据中心常用的冷却设备）和 HVAC 系统。顺便说一下，所有这些都在互联网上。”

此次谈话是在最近发生的一波大规模宕机事件（其中包括涉及 Microsoft Outlook 的宕机事件）的背景下进行的。其他涉及美国国家安全局 (NSA)、FFA 和苹果公司。人们担心这些中断是网络攻击造成的，尽管官员们否认了这些说法。尽管如此，人工智能辅助网络攻击的现实正在促使公司寻找新的漏洞发现和修复策略。
纳德拉简要谈到了最近的 Outlook 情况，指出全球造成的不便是“潜在错误”导致了“完美风暴”的结果。
“我们发布了事件响应，显然我们将吸取所有的经验教训，包括上游架构和运营方面的经验教训，并解决这个问题，”他补充道。
“有人告诉我甚至是运输系统以及可发现但固件无法修补的东西的数量，”纳德拉还补充道，关于易受攻击的系统的话题。 “所以我们肯定必须真正实现现代化……然后我们必须评估威胁向量是什么样的，我们自己实时检测和防御的能力是什么样的。”
纳德拉还提出了更广泛的观点，即修补软件漏洞的过程已经升级，以适应潜在利用的速度，但这也导致了更多问题。
“我们现在拥有一个非常强大的工具来发现漏洞，”他说。然而，他说，公司过去有更多的时间来测试这些补丁、了解情况并部署它们。与此同时，人工智能使复杂的网络攻击变得更容易实施。
“补丁[现在]需要立即从可用到在生产中进行修补，因为它正在被广泛利用，对吧？所以这会造成不稳定。”

fulltext: Google is trying to force Gemini on schools, and they’re not thrilled.

New York, Los Angeles, and Chicago schools are considering Google alternatives after the company said it will disable Search for schools that opt out of its AI features, according to The New York Times. Starting next year, schools will not have the option to disable Gemini-powered features without also disabling Search. Chris Phillips, Google’s vice president of education, told the Times that, “Search and AI are deeply integrated,” and that schools that turn off Google’s AI features “will not have access to Search.”

Many elected officials, including New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Senator Bernie Sanders, responded harshly, calling Google’s behavior “extortion.” Mamdani had recently announced a policy that barred 2-K-8 students from using AI in the classroom. In a statement to the Times, New York City schools chancellor Kamar H. Samuels said, “If Google doesn’t reconsider their position, we will explore other search options.” Chicago’s public schools have also reportedly told Google that if it can’t provide a version of Search without AI, “the district will look to other search solutions.”

In a statement to The Verge, Google spokesperson Laura Breen said, “We hear parents and teachers’ concerns about students using AI to shortcut learning, and we share the same goal: help students learn. To improve Search for the classroom, we’re starting to pilot Guided Learning capabilities in Search this month to walk students step-by-step through a range of complex problems, instead of just giving quick answers. Next year, we’re also updating our approach to controls for schools to address feedback we’ve heard from educators, so Gemini app, Gemini Notebook and Search will be off by default until schools decide which services to enable. We are actively building these experiences in partnership with educators, listening closely to ensure our products support students and teachers.”

Educators are wary of AI’s effect on students’ critical thinking skills, and some studies have shown that students who use AI generally perform worse on tests. There are also concerns about the mental health effects on children who develop relationships with chatbots at a young age. But Google is deeply embedded in classrooms across the US, which rely on Google Classroom, Chromebooks, and other services, and going fully Google-free might prove difficult.

fulltext_cn: 谷歌正试图将 Gemini 强行引入学校，但他们并不高兴。
据《纽约时报》报道，在谷歌表示将禁用对选择退出其人工智能功能的学校的搜索后，纽约、洛杉矶和芝加哥的学校正在考虑谷歌的替代品。从明年开始，学校将无法选择在不禁用搜索的情况下禁用 Gemini 支持的功能。谷歌教育副总裁克里斯·菲利普斯 (Chris Phillips) 向《泰晤士报》表示，“搜索和人工智能深度融合”，关闭谷歌人工智能功能的学校“将无法使用搜索”。

包括纽约市市长佐兰·马姆达尼和参议员伯尼·桑德斯在内的许多民选官员做出了严厉回应，称谷歌的行为是“敲诈勒索”。 Mamdani 最近宣布了一项政策，禁止 2-K-8 学生在课堂上使用人工智能。纽约市学校校长卡马尔·塞缪尔斯 (Kamar H. Samuels) 在给《泰晤士报》的一份声明中表示，“如果谷歌不重新考虑他们的立场，我们将探索其他搜索选项。”据报道，芝加哥的公立学校还告诉谷歌，如果它无法提供没有人工智能的搜索版本，“该学区将寻求其他搜索解决方案。”

谷歌发言人劳拉·布林（Laura Breen）在给 The Verge 的一份声明中表示：“我们听到了家长和老师对学生使用人工智能快捷学习的担忧，我们有着共同的目标：帮助学生学习。为了改进课堂搜索，我们本月开始在搜索中试行引导式学习功能，引导学生逐步解决一系列复杂问题，而不是仅仅给出快速答案。明年，我们还将更新学校控制方法，以解决我们从教育工作者那里听到的反馈，因此 Gemini 应用程序，在学校决定启用哪些服务之前，Gemini Notebook 和搜索将默认关闭。我们正在与教育工作者合作积极构建这些体验，密切倾听以确保我们的产品为学生和教师提供支持。”
教育工作者对人工智能对学生批判性思维能力的影响持谨慎态度，一些研究表明，使用人工智能的学生通常在测试中表现较差。人们还担心在年轻时与聊天机器人建立关系的儿童的心理健康会受到影响。但谷歌已深深嵌入美国各地的课堂，这些课堂依赖谷歌课堂、Chromebook 和其他服务，完全脱离谷歌可能会很困难。

fulltext: Facing opposition at home, Trump is eyeing the former US colony to build chip fabs and data centers.

President Donald Trump was greeted by no less than five beauty queens when he landed in the Philippines on Tuesday, according to local news outlet Rappler. As he stepped onto the tarmac, a child handed him small US and Philippine flags. A band played “YMCA,” a staple at Trump rallies, as more girls in traditional bell-sleeved blouses and young men in wide-brimmed hats danced to the song.

Outside the airport, hundreds of protesters packed streets bearing signs — and at least one prop casket — saying “Trump out.” Others say “Reject Pax Silica,” the name for the US-led international initiative to secure chips and critical minerals used in the hardware fueling the AI boom.
Peace and prosperity for whom?

“Pax” comes from the Latin word for “peace, stability, and long-term prosperity,” the Pax Silica website proudly says. Yet the unspoken question — peace and prosperity for whom? — explains the whiplash between the Philippine government’s warm welcome of Trump and the public fury raging outside.

Trump says he wants to “win AI” — whatever that means. As such, the US needs data centers full of GPUs to do it. With Americans increasingly opposed to data centers and chip factories being built in their communities, the US is now recruiting less affluent nations to take up some of the slack. Lawmakers from both the US and the Philippines are promising a slice of the riches that advances in generative AI are supposed to create. And that’s supposed to be worth the land razed, homes destroyed, and natural resources lost in the name of technological progress. In the Philippines, that’s taking the shape of a proposed 1,620-hectare (4,000 acres) hub for chip factories, processing plants for critical minerals, and data centers.

At least two dozen countries have signed on to the Pax Silica initiative, and Trump was expected to pressure more to join while in the Philippines for events related to the Association of Southeast Asian Nations summit. With Pax Silica, the US aims to insulate itself from China’s dominance in manufacturing semiconductors and processing critical minerals needed to make those chips. Trump held a bilateral meeting with President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. Wednesday before heading to Shenzhen to meet with China’s President Xi Jinping and Russia’s President Vladimir Putin.

Philippine and US officials are expected to sign a framework agreement by the end of the year for the jointly developed Pax Silica Economic Security Zone. The details are still murky and shrouded in NDAs. The Philippines’ Bases Conversion and Development Authority (BCDA) overseeing the plan expects an economic boom from minerals processing and chip manufacturing, with perhaps a data center or two on site. Meanwhile, human rights advocates who oppose the project warn that it will displace Indigenous residents, cutting them off from water resources on which they rely.
“How do we give up our burial grounds, our church, our livelihood?”

“We do not want to give up our community,” Petronila Capiz-Muñoz, chieftain of the Indigenous Aeta Hungey tribe, told Human Rights Watch. “How do we give up our burial grounds, our church, our livelihood? This is where we source our water, this is where we plant.” Capiz-Muñoz said BCDA officials have told residents that they’ll need to relocate by December to make way for development. Small farmers are also afraid the semiconductor hub will push them off their lands, according to Lian Buan, Southeast Asia researcher at Human Rights Watch.
There are layers of land-grabbing to unpack here.

The Aeta are among the first people to inhabit the Philippines, believed to have arrived around 30,000 years ago. And yet the Aeta Hungey tribe has been trying since 1994 to secure an official certificate recognizing its ancestral domain in one of the areas now facing industrial development. But since the tribe hasn’t been granted that certificate, the BCDA can still claim the AI hub will be built “outside titled ancestral domains.”

The agency says the project will be on public land located at the former Clark Air Base built in the early 1900s when the Philippines was a US territory. The Philippine constitution now only allows its own citizens to own private land. But the BCDA can offer leases lasting as long as 99 years to foreign developers. The agency expects to rake in close to $1 billion USD (about 60 billion in PHP Peso) from lease income over the first 25 years.
There are layers of land-grabbing to unpack here

The BCDA was in talks with around 30 different companies interested in setting up shop in Clark’s proposed AI hub, then-BCDA President and CEO Joshua Bingcang told reporters in July. He couldn’t name names, he said, because of NDAs — creating the same kind of opacity that has turned Americans against data centers on their home turf.

He did mention, however, that an American energy company was conducting a feasibility study into building a liquefied natural gas (LNG) line and plant to meet the hub’s enormous electricity demand. Bingcang called LNG a clean fuel, but that’s provably false. LNG is primarily methane, a smog-forming pollutant that is an even more potent greenhouse gas than carbon dioxide.

Bingcang said in September that the Philippine government wanted to invite Nvidia, TSMC, and Apple. While one or two data center developers had expressed interest, according to Bingcang, most of the companies interested were “high tech” manufacturing firms. He has also described chip manufacturing as a “clean” industry, echoing corporate spin that’s been around since the start of Silicon Valley.

At the first chip fabs in California, workers — many of them Filipino immigrants — donned “bunny suits” to assemble sensitive chips in environmentally controlled “clean rooms.” Little did they know that the gear they wore offered little protection against the harsh chemicals used in manufacturing, which also leaked out of storage tanks to contaminate soil and groundwater. When studies came out in the ’90s documenting disproportionately high rates of miscarriages among workers, companies pledged to phase out some of the chemicals linked to reproductive health risks. Around the same time, chip manufacturing started to move out of the US to Asia, where similar health problems stemming from the same chemicals cropped up even decades later.

Chipmakers say their fabs have gotten much safer over the years, in part because more work is automated. Even so, the BCDA estimates that the AI hub will create up to 190,000 direct jobs. The BCDA, White House, and Philippine’s Malacañang Palace did not immediately respond to questions from The Verge.

“I don’t want to date myself, but I knew your parents very well. They were great,” Trump told President Marcos during his visit. Marcos’ parents are estimated to have stolen up to $30 billion from government coffers over decades of rule before a people power movement ousted the current president’s father from the same office in the 1980s. But public memory, it seems, can be short.

And skyrocketing demand for more powerful chips used for generative AI has raised fears among environmental and labor groups that history might repeat itself. Companies move fast and break things, leaving a toxic mess in their wake. And when Americans decide they’ve had enough in their own back yards, the industry sets up shop somewhere else where they think their customers aren’t paying attention and politicians are happy to look the other direction.

据当地新闻媒体 Rappler 报道，唐纳德·特朗普总统周二抵达菲律宾时受到了至少五位选美皇后的迎接。当他走上停机坪时，一个孩子递给他美国和菲律宾的小国旗。一支乐队演奏了特朗普集会上的主打歌曲《YMCA》，更多穿着传统喇叭袖衬衫的女孩和戴着宽边帽的年轻男子随着这首歌起舞。
机场外，数百名抗议者挤满街道，举着标语——至少还有一个道具棺——写着“特朗普下台”。其他人则说“拒绝 Pax Silica”，这是美国主导的一项国际倡议的名称，该倡议旨在保护推动人工智能繁荣的硬件中使用的芯片和关键矿物。
和平与繁荣为了谁？
Pax Silica 网站自豪地表示，“Pax”源自拉丁语，意思是“和平、稳定和长期繁荣”。然而，有一个不言而喻的问题——和平与繁荣属于谁？ ——解释了菲律宾政府对特朗普的热烈欢迎与外界肆虐的公众愤怒之间的激烈冲突。

特朗普表示，他想“赢得人工智能”——无论这意味着什么。因此，美国需要充满 GPU 的数据中心才能做到这一点。随着美国人越来越反对在自己的社区建立数据中心和芯片工厂，美国现在正在招募不太富裕的国家来填补部分空缺。美国和菲律宾的立法者都承诺从生成式人工智能的进步所创造的财富中分得一杯羹。这应该是值得以技术进步的名义夷为平地、摧毁房屋和损失自然资源的。在菲律宾，拟建占地 1,620 公顷（4,000 英亩）的芯片工厂、关键矿物加工厂和数据中心中心。
至少有二十几个国家签署了“二氧化硅和平倡议”，预计特朗普将在菲律宾参加与东南亚国家联盟峰会相关的活动时向更多国家施压，要求其加入。通过Pax Silica，美国旨在使自己免受中国在半导体制造和制造这些芯片所需的关键矿物加工方面的主导地位的影响。特朗普周三与小费迪南德·R·马科斯总统举行双边会晤，然后前往深圳会见中国国家主席习近平和俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京。
菲律宾和美国官员预计将在今年年底前签署共同开发 Pax Silica 经济安全区的框架协议。细节仍然模糊且笼罩在保密协议中。负责监督该计划的菲律宾基地转换和发展局 (BCDA) 预计矿物加工和芯片制造将带来经济繁荣，并可能在现场设立一两个数据中心。与此同时，反对该项目的人权倡导者警告说，该项目将导致原住民居民流离失所，切断他们赖以生存的水资源。
“我们如何放弃我们的墓地、我们的教堂、我们的生计？”
“我们不想放弃我们的社区，”原住民艾塔亨吉部落的酋长佩特罗尼拉·卡皮兹-穆尼奥斯告诉人权观察。 “我们如何放弃我们的墓地、我们的教堂、我们的生计？这是我们的水源，这是我们种植的地方。”卡皮兹-穆尼奥斯表示，BCDA 官员已告诉居民，他们需要在 12 月之前搬迁，以便为开发让路。人权观察组织东南亚研究员连布安 (Lian Buan) 表示，小农户还担心半导体中心会将他们赶出自己的土地。
这里有层层的土地掠夺需要解开。
艾塔人是最早居住在菲律宾的民族之一，据信他们于大约 3 万年前抵达菲律宾。然而，自 1994 年以来，Aeta Hungey 部落一直在努力获得一份官方证书，承认其祖先在目前面临工业发展的地区之一的领地。但由于该部落尚未获得该证书，BCDA 仍然可以声称人工智能中心将建在“有资格的祖先领域之外”。
该机构表示，该项目将位于前克拉克空军基地的公共土地上，该基地建于 1900 年代初，当时菲律宾还是美国领土。菲律宾宪法现在只允许本国公民拥有私人土地。但 BCDA 可以向外国开发商提供长达 99 年的租约。该机构预计前 25 年将从租赁收入中赚取近 10 亿美元（约合 600 亿菲律宾比索）。
这里有层层的土地掠夺需要解开
BCDA 时任总裁兼首席执行官 Joshua Bingcang 在 7 月份告诉记者，BCDA 正在与大约 30 家有兴趣在克拉克拟建的人工智能中心开设店铺的公司进行谈判。他说，由于保密协议，他无法点名——这造成了同样的不透明性，这种不透明性曾让美国人反对他们家乡的数据中心。
不过，他确实提到，一家美国能源公司正在就建设液化天然气（LNG）管道和工厂进行可行性研究，以满足该枢纽巨大的电力需求。冰仓称液化天然气为清洁燃料，但事实证明这是错误的。液化天然气主要是甲烷，这是一种形成烟雾的污染物，是一种比二氧化碳更有效的温室气体。
冰仓9月份表示，菲律宾政府希望邀请英伟达、台积电和苹果。冰仓表示，虽然一两家数据中心开发商表达了兴趣，但大多数感兴趣的公司都是“高科技”制造公司。他还将芯片制造描述为一个“干净”的行业，这与硅谷诞生以来一直存在的企业运作相呼应。

在加利福尼亚州的第一家芯片工厂，工人（其中许多是菲律宾移民）穿着“兔子服”，在环境受控的“洁净室”中组装敏感芯片。他们几乎不知道，他们所穿的装备几乎无法抵御制造过程中使用的刺激性化学物质，这些化学物质也会从储罐中泄漏出来，污染土壤和地下水。上世纪 90 年代的研究表明，工人的流产率异常高，公司承诺逐步淘汰一些与生殖健康风险相关的化学物质。大约在同一时间，芯片制造开始从美国转移到亚洲，几十年后，同样的化学品引起的类似健康问题也出现了。
芯片制造商表示，多年来他们的工厂变得更加安全，部分原因是更多的工作实现了自动化。即便如此，BCDA 估计人工智能中心将创造多达 19 万个直接就业岗位。 BCDA、白宫和菲律宾马拉干鄢宫没有立即回应 The Verge 的提问。
“我不想和自己约会，但我很了解你的父母。他们很棒，”特朗普在访问期间告诉马科斯总统。据估计，在人民力量运动于 20 世纪 80 年代将现任总统的父亲赶下马科斯的父亲之前，马科斯的父母在数十年的统治中从政府金库中窃取了高达 300 亿美元。但公众记忆似乎很短暂。
对用于生成人工智能的更强大芯​​片的需求猛增，引起了环境和劳工组织的担忧，担心历史可能会重演。公司行动迅速，打破陈规，留下了有毒的烂摊子。当美国人认为他们在自己的后院已经受够了时，该行业就会在其他地方开设商店，他们认为他们的顾客没有注意到，而政客们则乐于看向另一个方向。

cards.title: Palmer Luckey warns AI-powered cyberattacks are outpacing defenses: ‘It’s time to start running’

AI-powered cyberattacks are moving faster than outdated technology systems can defend against them, Palmer Luckey warned at The New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday. Addressing the recent spate of tech outages, the Oculus founder and Anduril Industries co-founder argued that older systems are struggling to keep pace with the new hacking capabilities enabled by AI and warned it was time to quicken the pace of securing our defenses.
“We’re seeing the natural effects of a lot of these advanced AI tools allowing for the creation of various exploits,” he said.

While government officials largely attributed the latest set of technical issues to companies rushing to patch their systems to protect against the new vulnerabilities AI has discovered, Luckey focused on the underlying security challenges facing organizations using outdated technology.

Luckey explained that U.S. adversaries are currently exploiting the mismatch between new attack capabilities and our defense capabilities. These attacks are being carried out for both strategic and financial reasons, and North Korea was particularly involved, he added.

The interviewer, Andrew Ross Sorkin, noted that U.S. Vice President J.D. Vance had canceled his appearance at the Times’ conference this week because of the recent tech outages, saying he now had to attend meetings about the matter.
Given the situation, Sorkin asked Luckey how worried we should be about all this.
“It depends on how well prepared you are,” was Luckey’s answer. (He then ominously warned, “You guys are going to find out what’s going on soon enough.”)
The tech executive argued that AI could ultimately give defenders the upper hand, but they’d have to move more quickly.

“In the long run, the advantages are going to accrue to the side that is most effectively using AI for defense,” Luckey said. “With the people who say that everything can be hacked — they are right, for now. That actually may be the case with certain new techniques that are coming along. But as of right now, there’s a mismatch between the attackers who are very fast-moving and using technology and old, outdated systems that are not able to adopt technology as quickly as it is developed,” Luckey continued.
“And I think … people are going to have to pick up the pace,” he said. “It’s time to start running.”

周三，帕尔默·拉基 (Palmer Luckey) 在《纽约时报》DealBook 峰会上警告称，人工智能驱动的网络攻击的传播速度快于过时的技术系统所能防御的速度。针对最近发生的一系列技术中断问题，这位 Oculus 创始人兼 Anduril Industries 联合创始人认为，旧系统正在努力跟上人工智能带来的新黑客功能，并警告说是时候加快保护我们防御的步伐了。
“我们看到许多先进人工智能工具的自然效果，允许创建各种漏洞，”他说。
虽然政府官员主要将最新的一系列技术问题归因于公司急于修补系统以防止人工智能发现的新漏洞，但拉基关注的是使用过时技术的组织所面临的潜在安全挑战。
拉基解释说，美国的对手目前正在利用新的攻击能力与我们的防御能力之间的不匹配。他补充说，这些袭击是出于战略和财务原因，朝鲜尤其参与其中。
采访者安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金 (Andrew Ross Sorkin) 指出，由于最近的技术中断，美国副总统 J.D. 万斯 (J.D. Vance) 取消了本周出席《泰晤士报》会议的计划，并表示他现在必须参加有关此事的会议。
鉴于这种情况，索金问拉基我们应该对这一切感到多么担心。
“这取决于你准备得有多充分，”拉基的回答是。 （然后他不祥地警告说：“你们很快就会知道发生了什么。”）
这位技术高管认为，人工智能最终可以让防御者占据上风，但他们必须更快地采取行动。
拉基说：“从长远来看，最有效地利用人工智能进行防御的一方将获得优势。” “那些说一切都可以被黑客攻击的人——就目前而言，他们是对的。对于某些即将出现的新技术来说，实际上可能就是这种情况。但截至目前，行动迅速、使用技术的攻击者与无法像技术开发一样快地采用技术的陈旧、过时的系统之间存在着不匹配，”Luckey 继续说道。
“我认为……人们将不得不加快步伐，”他说。 “是时候开始跑步了。”
